Common genetic polymorphisms affect the human requirement for the nutrient choline

FASEB J. Author manuscript; available in PMC: 2006 Sep 25.

Abstract

Humans eating diets deficient in the essential nutrient choline can develop organ dysfunction. Fifty-seven humans were fed a low choline diet until they developed organ dysfunction or for up to 42 days.

Keywords: choline deficiency, PEMT

MATERIALS AND METHODS

Healthy males (n=31) and females (n=35) were recruited by advertising. They ranged in age from 18 to 70 years and had body mass indices between 19 and 33. Of the originally recruited 66 subjects, 61 completed at least the initial phase and the depletion phase.

Genotyping

Peripheral lymphocytes were isolated from blood by Ficoll-Hypaque gradient and genomic DNA extracted according to the manufacturer's instructions. SNP analyses were carried out by DNA sequencing of PCR products.

RESULTS

In all women, 18 of the 23 (78%) carriers of the PEMT -744C allele (rs12325817) developed organ dysfunction when fed a low choline diet (odds ratio 25, P=0.002; Table 3). There was no effect in men.

DISCUSSION

Common genetic polymorphisms have been reported to influence human requirements for nutrients. While a larger study is needed to confirm these findings, it does appear that these polymorphisms influence the susceptibility to developing organ dysfunction when fed a low choline diet.
